condition: pediatric button battery ingestion in a 3-year-old child who swallowed a coin-sized lithium battery from a television remote
level_rationale: Swallowing a coin-sized lithium button battery from a television remote 20 minutes ago in a 3-year-old child is a time-critical pediatric emergency because esophageal lithium battery impaction can generate mucosal hydroxide burns and perforation within 2 hours, requiring immediate emergency department radiographs and emergent endoscopic removal, whereas swallowing 1 soft ripe raspberry off a snack plate in the living room is harmless food intake requiring no medical care.

design_note: Uses three strictly atomic reference facts (3-year-old daughter, in the living room 20 minutes ago, and swallowing a coin-sized lithium button battery from the TV remote) with zero apostrophe contractions and an exact 10-word vs 10-word span swap. Placing the swallowed object cleanly in f3 avoids stranding chest pain or drooling when f3 shifts under Rule A and Rule D to swallowing 1 soft ripe raspberry (level 4 ER to level 1 home self-care) with zero stated negatives.
